title: How Picou learned and composed the blues
summary: Picou claims to be first to compose the blues, telling how he and bassist Jimmy Brown heard a railroad work gang singing and made it into a tune in the District.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. When did you first hear the blues? Did you, when you were a boy, did they sing the blues or play the blues on the instruments? When you were a boy learning on guitar? I was the first man that composed the blues. I used to play by Billy Phillips on Zero and Aberdeen. Now, I'll tell you how I learned the blues. Me and my friend, Jimmy Brown, that used to be in our band, and he used to be the bass player. So he had a woman that used to come on the piano. We had a piano. So one day he told me, say, Pike, I want you to come with me. I said, where? Come on. I went with him on the railroad on the front by the river. And that time, he was putting up a track. You know? And they had one band that was singing the blues. You know? I said, Pike, listen right there. I said, see, they sound good at you. The blues, he was singing the blues. I said, listen. He said, could you do something with that? I said, sure. I said, I got that back down. He says to me, well, I'll tell you. I said, do you know the words of, oh, he said, I got that. Oh, so we got everything. So I went at my house. We're here. I took my piano. And I blow that melody for him. And then he said, and that night, we went, because we had a steady job, you know, for a life. And that night, we put it on. There's where the blues comes from. Who's coming from? First time. That was in the district then. In the district. That was the district.
